Bill Clinton. Born in nineteen forty-six, Clinton was the forty-second President of the United States, serving from nineteen ninety-three to two thousand and one. The first president born after World War Two and the second to face impeachment, he presided over the post-Cold War era, economic prosperity, and a series of foreign interventions in the Balkans and elsewhere.

Clinton served as Governor of Arkansas from nineteen seventy-nine to eighty-one and again from nineteen eighty-three to ninety-two. He portrayed himself as a New Democrat bridging old party divisions and won the nineteen ninety-two election with forty-three percent of the vote against an incumbent George H.W. Bush weakened by recession. He signed the North American Free Trade Agreement, or NAFTA, in nineteen ninety-three, expanding continental trade and becoming a pillar of his economic agenda, though it angered labor unions. He passed the Family and Medical Leave Act, expanded the Earned Income Tax Credit, and signed welfare reform in nineteen ninety-six that replaced guaranteed assistance with time limits and work requirements, reflecting his New Democrat pragmatism.

Clinton presided over a period of economic expansion, budget surpluses, and declining unemployment. The dot-com boom created a sense of prosperity, though underlying financial risks accumulated. He intervened militarily in Somalia from nineteen ninety-two to ninety-three, Bosnia in nineteen ninety-five, and Kosovo in nineteen ninety-nine, establishing a pattern of humanitarian and strategic interventionism but with mixed results and criticism of American imperialism. He failed to respond effectively to the Rwandan genocide in nineteen ninety-four, a humanitarian catastrophe in which eight hundred thousand Tutsi were killed. His inaction became a defining regret.

Clinton conducted an affair with White House intern Monica Lewinsky from nineteen ninety-five to ninety-seven. He denied it under oath, saying "I did not have sexual relations." He was impeached by the House in nineteen ninety-eight for perjury and obstruction of justice but acquitted by the Senate. He was re-elected in nineteen ninety-six with forty-nine percent of the vote and left office with high approval ratings despite the scandal, with the economy still expanding.
